title: p0049
universal_lens: Biological spatial reception and adaptive behavior are unified as a multi-modal sensory fusion problem. Vestibular, proprioceptive, and olfactory inputs form a high-dimensional state vector, integrated via non-linear operators to estimate environmental gradients and kinematic trajectories within a constrained topological manifold.
gsi_mapping: Sensory receptor responses map directly to Bayesian likelihood functions over spatial priors. Olfactory intensity decays with distance, providing probabilistic constraints on target location. GSI utilizes conformal inference to bound the uncertainty of these multi-sensory estimates under noisy atmospheric diffusion conditions.
gse_mapping: The cerebellum acts as a continuous Kalman filter, fusing labyrinthine angular velocity and neck proprioception to update the organism's kinematic state. GSE models this as a Markov Decision Process where spatial relationships dictate optimal control policies for survival and navigation.

Failure modes arise when the underlying assumptions of smooth diffusion or rigid biomechanics break down, leading to singularities in the control policy.
